dedupe_keys.name: elmfire eulerian level set model of fire spread

description: ELMFIRE is an operational wildland fire spread model used by fire agencies, researchers and engineers to simulate how wildfires grow across real landscapes. It couples the Rothermel and Canadian (CFFDRS) surface spread formulations with a level-set front-tracking method, and adds crown fire, ember spotting, suppression (initial and extended attack), structure-to-structure fire spread in the wildland-urban interface, smoke emissions for the HYSPLIT dispersion model and a Monte Carlo mode for annual burn probability. Chris Lautenberger develops it, and through the Pyrecast project it forecasts the spread of most large fires in the continental United States. Coverage is any landscape for which gridded fuels, topography, weather and moisture are supplied as GeoTIFF rasters; resolution is set by the input grid. Outputs are georeferenced rasters of time of arrival, spread rate, fireline intensity and flame length. It is Fortran source code on GitHub, parallelised with MPI and runnable from a laptop to a cluster or in Docker, with a full user guide, tutorials and verification cases. Licence: GNU AGPL v3 with the Commons Clause, so it is free to use but may not be sold; no fee. Caveats: the build targets Linux, real fuel and weather inputs come through the CloudFire data services, and fire behaviour models carry large uncertainty. Simulation uses: wildfire hazard exposure of infrastructure and communities, real-time forecasting for emergency response, and risk assessment. Related wildfire spread models in the register: Cell2Fire and the USDA Missoula Fire Lab tools.
